metadata.name: apt-get
metadata.displayName: apt-get - APT package handling utility (command-line tool)

installation.note: apt-get is part of the apt package management system, installed by default on all Debian/Ubuntu systems

overview.summary: The apt-get command is a powerful package management tool for Debian and Ubuntu systems. It handles installation, removal, and updates of software packages from repositories. While 'apt' is the newer recommended command, apt-get remains widely used and is the foundation of package management on Ubuntu systems.

syntax.description: apt-get requires a command (like install, update, upgrade) and optionally package names. Most operations require root privileges.

misconceptions.title: apt vs apt-get
misconceptions.misconception: apt and apt-get are completely different
misconceptions.reality: apt is a newer, user-friendly command that combines apt-get and apt-cache functionality. Both work, but 'apt' is recommended for interactive use.
misconceptions.tip: Use 'apt' for interactive use, 'apt-get' is still fine and often used in scripts

misconceptions.title: Update vs Upgrade
misconceptions.misconception: update and upgrade do the same thing
misconceptions.reality: update refreshes package lists, upgrade actually installs updates. Always run 'update' before 'upgrade'.
misconceptions.tip: Think of it as: update = refresh the menu, upgrade = order the new items

common_pitfalls.description: Trying to install packages without updating package lists first
common_pitfalls.solution: Always run 'sudo apt-get update' before installing or upgrading packages
Always use 'sudo' with apt-get commands (except 'apt-get help')

common_pitfalls.description: remove keeps config files, purge removes everything
common_pitfalls.solution: Use 'remove' to keep configs, 'purge' for complete removal

common_pitfalls.description: Installation fails due to dependency conflicts
common_pitfalls.solution: Run 'sudo apt-get -f install' to fix broken dependencies

related_commands.description: apt is the newer recommended command that combines apt-get and apt-cache
apt-cache searches and shows package information, often used with apt-get
dpkg is the low-level package manager that apt-get uses
snap is an alternative package manager for snap packages

best_practices: Use 'apt' command for interactive use (newer, better UX)
Use '-s' to simulate before making changes
Regularly run 'apt-get update && apt-get upgrade' to keep system updated
Use 'autoremove' periodically to clean up unused packages
Use 'clean' to free up disk space from package cache
Read prompts carefully before confirming installations
performance_tips: Running 'update' regularly keeps package lists fresh and speeds up searches
Use 'apt' instead of 'apt-get' for slightly better performance in some cases
Cleaning cache with 'apt-get clean' can free significant disk space

additional_notes.ubuntu_specific: apt-get is the standard package manager for Ubuntu and Debian systems
additional_notes.repositories: Packages come from repositories defined in /etc/apt/sources.list
additional_notes.modern_alternative: The 'apt' command is recommended for interactive use, but apt-get is still widely used and supported
